angle: While digital communication lacks the non-verbal cues found in face-to-face interaction and may compromise the understanding of emotions, virtual environments also offer specific domains for non-verbal interaction and therapeutic tools for social training.
title: The Erosion of Social Cues

verdict: The evidence confirms that digital communication lacks real-time non-verbal cues which can hinder emotional understanding, but it also shows that technology is being developed to simulate or facilitate these interactions.
caveat: The sources provide a mix of literature reviews and theoretical premises rather than experimental data measuring the specific degradation of real-world intuition.
caption:
Digital communication changes how you perceive the emotions of others.

Research shows that a lack of non-verbal cues in digital messages can influence your understanding of attitudes. However, technology is also being developed as a tool for social training and moral reasoning. The evidence on the specific degradation of real-world intuition is currently mixed and relies on theoretical premises.
